payload.name: Aesthetic-Usability Effect
payload.fact: Controlling for processing fluency considerably diminishes (but does not eliminate) the correlation between aesthetics and usability judgments, indicating fluency is a contributing third variable.
payload.boundary: Controlling for fluency considerably diminishes the correlation between aesthetics and usability.

provenance.title: Statistically Controlling for Processing Fluency Reduces the Aesthetic-Usability Effect
provenance.quote_or_locus: When controlling for fluency, however, the aesthetic-usability effect was considerably diminished; the correlation decreased to .34

payload.grade_basis: Mechanical single-source grade cap (owner rule, 2026-08-10): 1 source -> C+ max, 2 sources -> B- max, 3+ independent sources -> B max, A band only with a meta-analysis or replication in the cited set.
